a: Up to $150,000 direct costs for joint Yale-UConn teams, or up to $75,000 for single-institution teams; performance period Jan 11 - Dec 31, 2027
dt: Full proposals due Nov 30, 2026 at 12 noon via the QuantumCT submission portal; results expected the week of Jan 11, 2027
e: Pilot grants funded by the NSF Engine award to QuantumCT for use-inspired quantum sensing research: magnetic-aided inertial navigation, Rydberg-atom RF detection, quantum-enabled distributed sensing, and quantum processes in biological systems. Projects must be led by tenure-track or tenured Yale or UConn faculty and include an unfunded industry partner; joint Yale-UConn teams are preferred.
f: QuantumCT (NSF Regional Innovation Engine, Yale and UConn)
n: QuantumCT Use-Inspired Research Pilot Grants: Quantum Sensing (Fall 2026)
